source.contest: UKMT Senior Team Maths Challenge (Regional Final)

prompt:
Complete the crossnumber in the figure. Each white square holds one digit, and the number of digits of each answer is given in brackets. Answers to some clues are needed for other clues.

**Across**

- **1.** The product of the digits in 5 Down (2)
- **7.** A multiple of $3^2$ and $p^2$, where $p$ is a single-digit prime and $p\neq3$ (5)
- **8.** $x$, where $x+\frac12y=19\text{ Down}+1$ and $2x-\frac14y=10\text{ Across}-1$ (3)
- **9.** A solution of $x^2-18x-14\text{ Across}=0$ multiplied by 6 Down $\div10$ (4)
- **10.** The interior angle, in degrees, of a regular polygon with 120 sides (3)
- **12.** The mean of this number, 19 Down and 23 Across is 5 Down (3)
- **14.** $\sqrt{2\text{ Down}}+19\text{ Down}$ (3)
- **15.** A palindromic prime (3)
- **17.** $n^n$, where $n$ is a positive integer (4)
- **21.** The shortest side in a right-angled triangle with sides 20 Down and $13^2$ (3)
- **22.** $(40^3+40^2)+(40^2+40)$ (5)
- **23.** $19\text{ Down}\div\sqrt[4]{81}$ (2)

**Down**

- **2.** $n^{n^2-1}$, where $n$ is a positive integer (4)
- **3.** A palindromic number that is divisible by 11 (5)
- **4.** $(70^3-70^2)-(70^2-70)$ (6)
- **5.** $10\text{ Across}\div\sqrt[4]{\frac{81}{256}}$ (3)
- **6.** A solution of $x^2+2x-13\text{ Down}=0$ multiplied by 23 Across (3)
- **9.** Twice 15 Across (3)
- **11.** A multiple of 7 whose digits are those of 10 Across together with those of 15 Across (6)
- **13.** The mean of this number, 10 Across and 23 Across is 19 Down (3)
- **16.** 100 multiplied by the largest prime factor of 11 Down (5)
- **18.** $12\text{ Across}\times\sqrt[5]{17\text{ Across}}+\sqrt[5]{17\text{ Across}}$ (4)
- **19.** The interior angle, in degrees, of a regular polygon with 20 sides (3)
- **20.** $y$, where $x+\frac12y=19\text{ Down}+1$ and $2x-\frac14y=10\text{ Across}-1$ (3)

solutions.title: Work through the clues
solutions.body:
**Clues that stand alone.** 10A: a regular 120-gon has exterior angle $3^\circ$, so the interior angle is $177$. 19D: the 20-gon has exterior angle $18^\circ$, interior $162$. 23A $=162\div3=54$. 22A $=(64000+1600)+(1600+40)=67240$. 4D $=(343000-4900)-(4900-70)=333270$. 17A $=n^n$ with four digits: $5^5=3125$. 2D $=n^{n^2-1}$ with four digits: $3^8=6561$.

**Clues that follow.** 5D $=177\div\frac34=236$, so 1A $=2\cdot3\cdot6=36$. 12A: $\frac{12A+162+54}3=236$ gives 12A $=492$. 13D: $\frac{13D+177+54}3=162$ gives 13D $=255$. 14A $=\sqrt{6561}+162=81+162=243$. 6D: $x^2+2x-255=0$ has solution $x=15$, so 6D $=15\cdot54=810$. 9A: $x^2-18x-243=0$ has solution $x=27$, so 9A $=27\cdot810\div10=2187$. 18D $=492\cdot5+5=2465$ (since $\sqrt[5]{3125}=5$).

**The simultaneous equations (8A, 20D).** $x+\frac y2=163$ and $2x-\frac y4=176$. Doubling the second, $4x-\frac y2=352$; adding to the first gives $5x=515$, $x=103$, then $y=120$. So 8A $=103$ and 20D $=120$.

**21A.** The triangle has sides $120$ and $169$; if $169$ is the hypotenuse the third side is $\sqrt{169^2-120^2}=119$, which is the shortest side.

**Using crossings.** 15A is a palindromic prime whose middle digit (the last digit of 4D $=333270$) is $0$, so it is $a0a$; since $a0a=101a$ is prime only for $a=1$, 15A $=101$ and 9D $=202$. 3D is a five-digit palindrome whose last three digits are $1,7,1$ (crossing 8A, 9A, 10A), so it is $17171=11\cdot1561$. 11D uses the digits of $177$ and $101$ and its first digit is the last digit of 10A: $717101=7\cdot102443$. Its largest prime factor is $139$ ($717101=7\cdot11\cdot67\cdot139$), so 16D $=13900$. 7A has the form $3a3b1$ from crossings; being a multiple of $9$ forces $a+b\in\{2,11\}$ and being a multiple of $p^2$ for $p=2,5,7$ leaves only $31311=9\cdot7^2\cdot71$.

All 24 clues check out in the completed grid shown in the answer.
